recipes.name: Chef John’s Caramel Chicken
ingredients_raw: 2 fresh jalapeno peppers, seeded and sliced

steps.text: Whisk brown sugar, water, fish sauce, rice wine vinegar, garlic, soy sauce, and ginger together in a bowl until brown sugar completely dissolved, about 1 minute; set aside.
Heat oil in a skillet over high heat; add chicken.
Pour 1/3 cup brown sugar mixture over chicken; cook and stir until mixture has a syrup-like consistency, 6 to 7 minutes.
Pour in remaining brown sugar mixture; cook until chicken tender and no longer pink inside, about 5 minutes.
Stir in in peanuts, green onions, and jalapeños; cook until warmed through, 2 to 3 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Chef John’s Caramel Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Succulent chicken cooked in a spicy sweet-sour sauce. It’s inspired by a dish made famous by San Francisco’s The Slanted Door restaurant.

review.reviewBody: Just made this for dinner tonight. Delicious! I wasn't prepared to make it, so had to do some substitutions. (White onions for green onions, more soy sauce for the fish sauce) Even with the substitutions, this spicy dish was superb served over brown rice.

One of best chicken dishes ever! I did use red pepper flakes instead of jalapeno - but really that was just a visual difference.
I used garlic paste - per Chef John's video. I also poured about 1/2 sauce in with chicken and reduced it down till nothing in the pan - it was all caramelized on the chicken and then added the rest. It cooked down very fast after that and fresh green onions on at the very end makes a wonderful statement in flavor. Don't skimp on them. I also took advice and kept the pan on high heat. We served with roasted garlic cauliflower so did not miss the rice at all. I can't wait to have left overs and will keep these ingredients on hand to make any time. It will impress your guests!

This recipe makes a delicious sauce. I made this twice as per the recipe and the third time I altered the technique. It is all about the caramel here folks. I cooked down all of the brown sugar mixture first until all of it became a thick bubbly very hot caramelized syrup. Then I threw the chicken into the syrup to cook it. I got a much thicker, coated mahogany chicken than the original recipe.

Fantastic! Doubled everything, used more garlic and threw in 3 multi-colored peppers in during that last step so they can cook in the sauce for 3 minutes. Served over white rice... and I like to put a few carrot chips on top for more color and vegetables. Very, very good. Made twice now and will make again!

Watching the video and comparing how much liquid I had - seems measurements might be off in recipe. He had FAR less liquid in pan. Agree with others - omit the water. I’m je doesn’t say if the sugar should be packed. I had a hard time getting to syrup stage. Could be two things - 1) sugar was supposed to have been jacked or 2) I didn’t siens enough time dissolving the sugar with whisk so when I added the first 1/3 cup it had more liquid than sugar (sugar would have sunk to bottom of bowl). Took more than twice as long to get to syrup stage. I was cooking in my le creuset. It eventually got almost there but not quite. Again- way more liquid in my pan than his. After adding remaining liquid it took a little longer than recipe stayed to get to caramélisation. I would say totally caramelized but close. This is a very sweet dish on its own. I think when I serve over rice it will be perfect and that will cut some sweetness. It’s a bit sweet for my taste but I’m making this for others who I think will love it. The flavors are there. Just a tad sweet but again - it’s caramélisés chicken what do you expect lol. I’ve cooked at least thirty chef John recipes. All 5 star. I’ve never had issues with technique before. His recipes are foolproof. This one is a bit trickier. This is why I’m giving 4 stars. I’d say my cooking level is quite advanced and I got tripped up a bit but adjusted on the fly. Luckily chicken thighs are forgiving as mine needed much more time.
I made a noodle bowl out of this with yakisoba noodles, carrot, cucumber, chopped peanuts, jalapeno, green onions, and cilantro. It was very good.

Fantastic flavor in the end. First time I made it, it would not thicken in the carmelization process, so I tweeked recipe to include cornstarch. Second time, I definitely decreased fish
sauce to 1/4 c as it was too salty. AND I decided to watch the video on advice of one of the reviewers, and it varies from recipe instructions in a detrimental way. Third time was a charm, extremely fantastic palette of flavors. Of course rice, and baked veggies as side. MMMMMM

awesome! just made this using the 6 serving list and this is excellent. Just as Chef John detailed in his video....easy to make too. I cut up chicken, onions, jalapenos earlier in the day to save some time but it's really not that involved anyway. 
I even used low salt peanuts and low sodium soy sauce just to keep salt content as low as possible and served over rice.

A keeper.

This is a very versatile Wednesday night recipe when time is short, weather is hot, and you don't want takeout! It has nice flavor even without the peppers. I added sautéed sweet onion and baby Bella mushrooms, but carrots work well. Also suggest a half teaspoon of white pepper. A definite keeper! Thanks Chef!

I tried this recipe for the first time tonight and, as always with Chef John's recommendations, it’s definitely a keeper! I made a few small tweaks based on what I had on hand. I used jarred jalapeño slices and honey-flavored dry roasted peanuts, and I skipped the cilantro. One thing I changed, based on other reviews, was leaving out about half a cup of the brown sugar mixture, thinking it might be too watery. That turned out to be unnecessary— the dish could have easily absorbed it all. I believe the problem some people had with thickening comes from not having the pan hot enough. I kept mine at around 8-9, and it caramelized perfectly. I did cook the chicken a couple of minutes longer to ensure it was done and crispy. Overall, it’s fairly easy to prepare, and I’ll definitely be making this again!

Super crazy easy and really good flavor! I added a tablespoon of tapioca starch after adding the remaining sauce to the chicken, and the sauce thickened beautifully. The peanuts and green onions add a great texture to it, too.
Absolutely enjoyed this flavorful dish. I added cilantro rice on the side with roasted broccoli and cauliflower. Uh-MAY-ziiinngggg!!!!

Really excellent. My sons are coming to visit and asked me to make the recipe again - a winner. Only thing I do different - at the end of the recipe I remove the food from the pan, throw in a little bit of corn starch, then put all the stuff back in.
Loved this recipe from Chef John! It is fantastic without any changes.

Chef John always makes easy good recipes. This recipe was no different. Very good. I followed the recipe as is for the most part. I did pour the remaining sauce in the skillet with the chicken but removed the chicken prior to the green onions and peanuts. I didn't want my chicken to dry out. Might of had the heat too hot. I did do the sauce on the side. Added the green onions and peanuts and mixed it into the sauce then poured the sauce over the chicken and garnished with a few green onions for the color. My husband loved it.. Gobbled it up. I'll do this one again.
I did NOT think buying fish sauce would be a worthwhile investment for my cooking, but my husband has asked for this dish now enough times to drain that first ever bottle. Great recipe! 👍
Chef John is amazing. I've made this recipe a few times. The sticky sweetness of the carmel chicken is soooo good! I love this!
It tasted very fishy. It would not thicken, so I had to add some cornstarch. But there was nothing caramel about the taste. Just fish
Different profiles but my sauce was very watery. Perhaps additional brown sugar to make it thicken up and the fish sauce made the kitchen smell
